label:
Drugs from
transgenic milk
note: The goats (and rabbits) carry a human gene.

about.text: Human proteins made in the milk of genetically modified animals and purified from it as medicines. The first approved was ATryn, an anticoagulant from goats' milk (2006); Ruconest, for hereditary angioedema, is made in rabbits' milk. Ruconest is made by the Dutch company Pharming.

sources.text: The milk of a few herds of transgenic goats and rabbits. My own rough estimate.

facts.v: ATryn (antithrombin alfa): transgenic goats. Ruconest (conestat alfa): transgenic rabbits
A human gene is joined to a milk-protein promoter, so the animal makes the human protein only in its mammary gland and secretes it into the milk
E. coli cannot add the sugar chains (glycosylation) C1-inhibitor needs; without them it clears from the blood quickly
Ruconest contains traces of rabbit protein; rabbit allergy is a contraindication
ATryn approved by FDA (2009); its EU authorisation has lapsed. Ruconest treats acute hereditary angioedema attacks
